 Senior Citizens League stimulus proposal: $1,400 checks for Social Security recipients
 Kendall Little · Senior Writer, Credit Cards Fri, November 20, 2026 at 1:54 PM MST 2 min read An advocacy group for American senior citizens is issuing a proposal for the incoming Congress: a one-time $1,400 stimulus to help seniors keep up with inflation. 
 The Senior Citizens League (TSCL) is an advocacy group representing older Americans. It is primarily focused on Social Security and Medicare benefits, as well as military and veteran benefits.  
 The stimulus proposal hasn't been introduced into any legislation, but the organization is turning to the incoming Congress for reform. 
 "The incoming class of Senators face an enormous responsibility," TSCL executive director Shannon Benton said in a statement. "Americans have chosen these elected representatives to protect seniors' dignity and rights, to protect benefits for today's retirees while reforming Social Security taxes to ensure the program continues to serve generations to come." 
 Learn more: October inflation breakdown: Cheaper gas, bigger grocery bills 
 What is the $1,400 stimulus for? 
 TSCL's proposed one-time $1,400 stimulus would go to all American retirees who receive Social Security benefits. The check, the group says, would "help make up for inadequate COLAs and rising inflation."  
 One reason seniors have been hit particularly hard by persistent inflation is rising medical costs. According to the most recent Consumer Price Index data, medical costs are still increasing. While prices increased by 0.4% overall month over month, medical care items increased by 0.5%, medical services increased by 0.3%, and hospital services increased by 0.8%.  
 At the same time, Medicare costs are also rising. Medicare Part B premiums will increase by $6.50 per month, or about 3.2% in 2027. The annual deductible for beneficiaries will increase by $9 in 2027. 
 The Senior Citizens League is issuing a proposal for the incoming Congress: a one-time $1,400 stimulus to help seniors better keep up with inflation. · mpi04/MediaPunch/MediaPunch/IPx To help offset inflation, the Social Security Administration already makes an annual cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for beneficiaries. The COLA for 2027 is 3.6% — the highest since 2023 and enough to add an average of $75 per month to the benefits seniors receive. 
 However, advocates say the COLA isn't enough to keep up , given factors like inflation and rising Medicare premiums. That's where the proposed stimulus can help, according to TSCL.  
 "This one-time, lump-sum, and tax-exempt payment would pay retirees back at least some of their Social Security benefits' lost value," Benton wrote in a statement . 
 Read more: Medicare changes coming in 2027 
 More proposed changes for seniors 
 The $1,400 senior stimulus is one part of a broader call to action TSCL is making to the incoming Congress. These are the other changes the group is advocating for: 
 Lift or eliminate the Social Security payroll tax threshold 
 Restore Medicare and Medicaid budget cuts from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) 
 Add coverage for dental, vision, and hearing to Medicare benefits
